title: Annotatio I §.IV IMPLICITE Lutheran: Luther’s duplex — in/cum/sub hoc pane (Schwärmer sermon)
pass_a_gloss: The more famous Lutheran interpretation of the proposition is twofold. One is Luther’s: This, or this bread, is my body — i.e. in, with, and under this bread is my body (Wittenberg Tom. II, sermon against the Fanatics, p. 98). Let them / the Schwärmer / (so he is used to nickname those with whom he is not ὁμοψῆφος in the sacramentarian controversy) fabren / and let us remain by the words as they sound: That IN THE BREAD the body of Christ and IN THE WINE His blood truly is.
pass_b_english: The better-known Lutheran reading of This is my body is twofold.
Luther’s: This / this bread is my body means in, with, and under this bread is my body (Wittenberg Tom. II vs the Fanatics, p. 98).
Let the Schwärmer go — his nickname for those not ὁμοψῆφος with him on the sacrament — and stay with the words as they sound: IN THE BREAD Christ’s body, IN THE WINE His blood truly.
source_text: LUTHERANORUM famosior propositionis interpretatio duplex est. Altera Lutheri: Hoc, seu hic panis, est corpus meum, i. e. in, cum & sub hoc pane est corpus meum, Tom. II. Witteberg. sermone contra Fanaticos pag. 98. Laß sie / die Schwärmer / (ita suo more cognominat eos quos non habet in controversia sacramentaria ὁμοψήφους) fabren / und laß uns bey den Worten bleiben wie sie lauten: Daß IM BROD der Leib Christi und IM WEIN warhafftig sein Blut sey.
